correctness.rationale: Replayed the frozen gray_paths_u16le.bin with the fresh verifier /workspace/branches/0376a469-53f7-424c-b1d9-a017debe03a4/independent_verify.py (python3, certificate path as its argument). I inspected the decisive code. The recursion tries every unused value subject exactly to the next alternating inequality, so its leaves are precisely all admissible permutations and in lexicographic order. Each fixed-size little-endian block has its entire index range as its index set, hence no omissions or duplicates, and each consecutive pair agrees outside two positions and has the two entries exchanged. All 103944 bytes were consumed: 5, 61, 1385, 50521 states and 4, 60, 1384, 50520 transitions (51968 total). SHA-256 a9fc613421c0eea64144092a959a85754da4fa1d16ceeba607f0611a17657b62 identifies the replayed input; legitimacy comes from the checked moves and exhaustive coverage, not the hash. The supplied two verifiers were read as evidence, not executed. The signs alternate at every edge, so odd vertex counts exclude a Hamilton cycle, not a path. This checks exactly the four stated sizes, not an all-even theorem or a generation algorithm.

The ranked-poset criterion summarized on p. 47 does not cover the even fence F_10: one terminal extremal element in each rank has only one cover in the relevant direction.
The p. 48 broader construction allows products of two adjacent transpositions.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither the odd construction nor the ranked-poset sufficient criterion supplies the finite even result. A double transposition may preserve sign, unlike every single transposition, and the allowed double moves cannot just be read as edges of the claimed graph.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Parity balance up to one is a necessary path condition in this bipartite graph, not a sufficient condition. A prism result or a path in a graph augmented with two-swap edges does not project to the frozen path.

value.rationale: The cutoff gives explicit positive cases for a documented even-size Gray-code question, including the full 50521-vertex n=10 graph. This is not a re-enumeration of zigzag numbers: the certificate witnesses a global ordering subject to a sharp single-move constraint and can be independently checked in full. The value is a reusable, meaningful finite benchmark, not a uniform construction or resolution of the general problem.
